_comment: The roles a list item's key or a draft item field can play, read from the words of its name (camelCase split, lower case), in priority order: a key's primary role is the first role any of its words names, a field may take each role its words name, in this order. A word may sit under several roles (`name` is an author or a title, `text` a quote or a description): lib/fill-list-content.mjs::matchFields gives a field a key whose primary role it plays first, and only when the block's item has none does a key that names the role later in this list take it (a team member's `name` takes a draft `title` when the item has no title key). An item key the block declares technical (block.json role `technical`) whose primary role is identity is the item's own name the block keys it by (an option picker skips an item with no `key`): lib/fill-list-content.mjs::identityKeys writes it from the item's words when the draft gives none. Read by lib/fill-list-content.mjs; data/item-roles.schema.json is its shape. A role with `takesUnmatched` is also the home of a draft field no other key matched by name or role: after both passes, an open string key of that role (a card's `subtitle`) takes the first such field (a count, a price note, a tag) whose own roles are none of `skipRoles` (a picture, a glyph, an address and an identity are never a subtitle); it never takes a field another key matches. Only one role may carry it.
